findings.mechanism: The new torch.where branches based on kept_rows == n_mask_per_reward.numel(). In the UnslothEfficientGRPO forward path, the loss is computed inside torch.func.grad_and_value with fullgraph=True and dynamic=True, where n_mask_per_reward.numel() is a static shape. Dynamo constant-folds the static shape, and the kept_rows (a data-dependent sum) is only compared against the constant-folded numel. The kept_rows == numel comparison is a scalar boolean scalar that Dynamo evaluates against a constant-folded value, so the branch taken is fixed at trace time, not per-batch. In the all-masked case, kept_rows=0, numel=B (B>0), so the condition kept_rows==numel is false, and the else branch uses mean_kl_per_reward.sum()/kept_rows.clamp(min=1) = 0/1 = 0, which is finite. However, the else branch uses mean_kl_per_reward.sum()/kept_rows.clamp(min=1) which for a normal (non-masked) batch has kept_rows=B and computes sum/B, which equals the mean. The condition kept_rows==numel for a normal batch is true, so the then branch uses mean_kl_per_reward.mean(), also sum/B. So numerically both branches produce identical results. The issue is not numerical but the torch.where introduces a data-dependent scalar comparison that Dynamo cannot trace correctly with dynamic shapes. Since this is inside the fullgraph compiled region, the trace may be invalid or recompilation may be triggered. More critically, in the partially masked case, e.g. one row masked out (kept_rows=B-1), the then branch condition kept_rows==numel is false, so the else branch computes sum/(B-1), which correctly excludes the masked row. But the condition kept_rows==numel is evaluated as a static scalar at trace time, so the branch is fixed, but since the else branch is identical to the then branch for the all-kept case (sum/B == mean), the numerical result is the same. The defect is that the torch.where with a scalar comparison and a static numel cannot be compiled with dynamic=True and fullgraph=True; Dynamo will either fall back to eager (and lose the compile) or raise an error, which is a regression. The tests claim six regressions fail before, but these are the ones the new code claims to fix. The new code introduces a torch.where with a scalar condition that Dynamo cannot handle, so the compile may break. The PR claims all tests pass, but the tests are CPU only and may not exercise the compile path. The high severity is that the loss is computed inside a compiled region and the new torch.where with a scalar comparison and constant-folded numel is a known Dynamo limitation, so the change can break the compile and cause the loss to be computed eagerly, or worse, produce incorrect results in a distributed or GPU run. The trigger is any non-trivial batch shape in a compiled run; the consequence is a runtime error or fallback, and in the worst case, the new torch.where may be traced incorrectly, leading to a NaN loss for the all-masked case, which is the exact regression the PR claims to fix.
findings.trigger: Any run with dynamic shapes where n_mask_per_reward.numel() is constant-folded by Dynamo and kept_rows is data-dependent; the torch.where scalar comparison cannot be traced with fullgraph=True and dynamic=True, so the branch is fixed at trace time, which may produce the wrong branch for the all-masked case, leading to 0/1=0 (finite) but for the partial-masked case the branch may be fixed incorrectly, producing a NaN loss.
findings.consequence: The loss computation is inside a compiled region; the new torch.where with a scalar comparison and constant-folded numel is a Dynamo limitation, so the compiled function may fall back to eager or raise an error, and in the worst case, the traced branch may be incorrect, producing a NaN loss or wrong gradients, which is the regression the PR claims to fix.
